questionText: Which of the following is a leap year?
hints: A leap year is divisible by 4. But century years (ending in 00) must be divisible by 400.
2024 is the only leap year.

stepByStep.text: Rule: divisible by 4 = leap. BUT century years must be divisible by 400.

misconceptions.A: 2023 is odd — can't be divisible by 4
misconceptions.B: 2100 is a century year and 2100 ÷ 400 ≠ whole number, so NOT a leap year
misconceptions.D: 1900 is a century year and 1900 ÷ 400 ≠ whole number, so NOT a leap year

questionText: How many days are there from 1st March to 1st May (including both dates)?
hints: Count the days in each month: March has 31 days, April has 30 days.
1 March to 31 March = 31 days. 1 April to 30 April = 30 days. Plus 1 May = 1 day.

misconceptions.A: Counted only March + April without May 1st: 31+29=60 (also wrong April days)

questionText: If 1st January 2023 was a Sunday, what day was 1st January 2024?
hints: 2023 is NOT a leap year, so it has 365 days. How many weeks is that?
365 ÷ 7 = 52 weeks and 1 extra day.
1 extra day means the day advances by 1: Sunday → Monday.

misconceptions.A: Forgot the extra day (assumed 365 = exact 52 weeks)
misconceptions.C: Advanced by 2 days (would be correct for a leap year)

questionText: If 1st January 2024 was a Monday, what day was 1st January 2025?
hints: 2024 IS a leap year (366 days). How many extra days beyond complete weeks?
366 ÷ 7 = 52 weeks and 2 extra days.
2 extra days: Monday + 2 = Wednesday.

misconceptions.A: Only advanced by 1 day (forgot it's a leap year with 366 days)

questionText: Republic Day 1993 was on Tuesday. On which day did it fall in 1997?
hints: Count odd days from 1993 to 1997. Normal year = 1 odd day. Leap year = 2 odd days.
1993: 1 day, 1994: 1 day, 1995: 1 day, 1996: 2 days (leap!). Total = 5 odd days.
Tuesday + 5 = Sunday.

stepByStep.text: Count from 26 Jan 1993 to 26 Jan 1997: 4 years.

misconceptions.B: Counted 4 odd days instead of 5 (missed the leap year extra day)

questionText: In 2007, Republic Day fell on Friday. On what day was it celebrated in 2008?
hints: 2007 is NOT a leap year. So 1st Jan to 1st Jan advances by 1 day.
But wait — is 2008 a leap year? Yes! Does the leap day (29 Feb) matter? Republic Day is 26 Jan, BEFORE Feb 29.
Since we're going from 26 Jan 2007 to 26 Jan 2008, and 2007 has 365 days: advance 1 day. Friday + 1 = Saturday.

misconceptions.D: Advanced by 2 (would apply if crossing a Feb 29)

questionText: If 14th February 1992 was a Friday, what day did 13th February 1993 fall on?
hints: 1992 is a leap year! From 14 Feb 1992 to 14 Feb 1993 = 366 days (crosses 29 Feb 1992).
366 ÷ 7 = 52 weeks + 2 days. So 14 Feb 1993 = Friday + 2 = Sunday.
But we want 13 Feb (one day BEFORE 14 Feb). Sunday − 1 = Saturday.

stepByStep.text: 1992 is a leap year. 14 Feb 1992 to 14 Feb 1993 = 366 days.

misconceptions.A: Forgot leap year (only advanced 1 day) and went back 1
misconceptions.D: Got 14 Feb 1993 = Sunday but forgot to go back 1 day to 13th

questionText: In a certain year, Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday occurred 5 times each in the month of July. Which date fell on a Sunday?
questionLatex: \text{July: Wed, Thu, Fri occur 5 times. Which date is Sunday?}
hints: July has 31 days = 4 weeks + 3 extra days. Those 3 extra days occur 5 times.
The 3 consecutive days that occur 5 times are Wed, Thu, Fri. So July 1st must be a Wednesday.
If July 1 = Wed, then Sundays fall on: 5, 12, 19, 26. Check which option matches.

stepByStep.text: 31 = 4×7 + 3. Three days occur 5 times. Those 3 days = Wed, Thu, Fri.
The first 3 days of the month = Wed, Thu, Fri. So July 1 = Wednesday.

questionText: How many odd days are there in 400 years?
hints: In 100 years: 76 normal years (76 odd days) + 24 leap years (48 odd days) = 124 odd days. But wait, century year might not be leap.
100 years = 5 odd days (after careful calculation). 400 years = 4 × 5 + 1 (extra leap from 400th year) = 20 + 1 = 21. 21 ÷ 7 = 3 weeks = 0 odd days.
400 years = 0 odd days! The calendar repeats exactly every 400 years.

stepByStep.text: This is a well-known calendar fact.
The calendar repeats exactly every 400 years.

misconceptions.A: 1 odd day is for 1 normal year, not 400
misconceptions.C: 3 odd days applies to a different calculation

questionText: A Cricket World Cup began on 17th March, Wednesday. The final match was on the second Sunday in May. On what date was the final?
hints: First find what day May 1st falls on. From 17 Mar (Wed) to 1 May: 14 (Mar) + 30 (Apr) + 1 = 45 days.
45 ÷ 7 = 6 weeks + 3 days. Wed + 3 = Saturday. So 1 May = Saturday.
If 1 May = Sat, then 2 May = Sun (1st Sunday). 9 May = Sun (2nd Sunday).

stepByStep.text: Days from 17 Mar to 1 May: Mar(14) + Apr(30) + May(1) = 45

questionText: In 2003, April Fools' Day (1st April) was on Tuesday. On which day was it celebrated in 2004?
hints: From 1 Apr 2003 to 1 Apr 2004: does it cross Feb 29?
Feb 2004 has 29 days (leap year). So 2003-2004 has 366 days from this April to next April.
Wait — count properly: Apr 2003 to Apr 2004 crosses Feb 2004. 366 days? No: it's 365 + 1 (for the leap day) = 366. 366 ÷ 7 = 52R2. Tuesday + 2 = Thursday.

stepByStep.text: 1 Apr 2003 to 1 Apr 2004 crosses Feb 29, 2004 (leap year).

misconceptions.D: Only advanced by 1 day (missed the leap year effect)

questionText: 9th April 1990 was a Monday. Which days occurred five times in that month?
questionLatex: \text{9 Apr 1990 = Mon. Which days occur 5 times?}
hints: April has 30 days = 4 weeks + 2 extra days. So exactly 2 days will occur 5 times.
If 9th = Monday, then 2nd = Monday, so 1st = Sunday. April starts on Sunday.
The first 2 days (Sunday and Monday) occur 5 times: Sundays on 1, 8, 15, 22, 29 and Mondays on 2, 9, 16, 23, 30.

stepByStep.text: April = 30 days = 4 weeks + 2 days. Two days occur 5 times.
9 Apr = Monday → 2 Apr = Monday → 1 Apr = Sunday
First 2 days of the month (Sun, Mon) occur 5 times.

misconceptions.B: Monday occurs 5 times but Tuesday only occurs 4 times
misconceptions.C: Only 2 days can occur 5 times in a 30-day month, not 3
misconceptions.D: The answer IS Sunday and Monday

questionText: A train departs at 09:45 and the journey takes 4 hours 35 minutes. At what time does it arrive?
hints: Add 4 hours 35 minutes to 9:45.
Hours: 9 + 4 = 13. Minutes: 45 + 35 = 80. But 80 minutes = 1 hour 20 minutes!
13 hours + 1 hour 20 minutes = 14:20 = 2:20 PM.

misconceptions.A: Forgot to carry the extra hour from 80 minutes
misconceptions.C: Wrote 1:80 PM — there's no such time! Minutes can't exceed 59.
misconceptions.D: This is actually the same answer in 24-hour format (14:20 = 2:20 PM)

questionText: Rahul celebrated his 5th birthday on 3rd August 2014 which was a Sunday. Which birthday will fall on Thursday?
questionLatex: \text{3 Aug 2014 = Sun. Which birthday on Thu?}
hints: Count odd days year by year from 2014. We need Thursday = Sunday + 4 days.
2014→2015: 1 odd day (Mon). 2015→2016: 2 odd days (Wed, crossing leap year). Total after 2 years = 3 days. 2016→2017: 1 odd day. Total = 4 days = Thursday!
3 Aug 2016 = 7th birthday. Wait, that's Wed. Let me recount. 2014(1)+2015(1)+2016(2) = 4 odd days. 2017 = 7th birthday = Thursday.

questionText: How many seconds are there in 2 hours?
hints: 1 hour = 60 minutes. 1 minute = 60 seconds.

2 hours = 2 × 3600 = 7200 seconds.

misconceptions.A: Only converted hours to minutes (2 × 60 = 120), not seconds
misconceptions.B: This is 1 hour in seconds, not 2

questionText: A normal year has how many odd days?
hints: A normal year has 365 days. Divide by 7 to find complete weeks and extra days.
365 ÷ 7 = 52 weeks + 1 day.
That 1 extra day is called 1 'odd day.' It's why the same date shifts by 1 day each normal year.

misconceptions.A: 0 odd days means the day wouldn't change year to year (only true for 400-year cycles)
misconceptions.C: 2 odd days is for a leap year (366 days)
misconceptions.D: 7 would mean 0 odd days (7 is a full week)

questionText: In the year 2000, Gandhi Jayanti (2nd October) fell on Monday. In which year was it first celebrated on Sunday after 2000?
hints: We need to go backwards 1 day from Monday = Sunday, which means we need total odd days = 6 (or 7−1).

Odd days: 2000(2, leap), 2001(1), 2002(1), 2003(1), 2004(2, leap). After 2000: 2 odd days → Wed. After 2001: +1=3 → Thu. After 2002: +1=4 → Fri. After 2003: +1=5 → Sat. After 2004: +2=7=0 → Mon again. Hmm.

Wait: 2000→2001: 2 Oct falls after Feb, so the leap year effect depends on position. 2000: advance 1 (Oct is after Feb, only 1 odd day from Oct to Oct in a year where the leap day is BEFORE). Mon+1=Tue(2001). +1=Wed(2002). +1=Thu(2003). +2=Sat(2004, leap year crossed). +1=Sun(2005). ✓
